title: Battle of the Atlantic
summary: The Battle of the Atlantic was the long Second World War campaign, from 3 September 1939 to 8 May 1945, to protect Allied shipping lines between North America and Britain from German U-boats. The Canadian War Museum counts more than 3,000 Allied ships lost, and the contest turned in the Allies' favour in May 1943.

uncertainty.note: Sources agree on September 1939 to May 1945. Veterans Affairs Canada gives exact dates; the Canadian War Museum and the Battle of the Atlantic Story page give months.

where.historical_name: North Atlantic sea lanes between North America and Britain

importance.justification: The longest campaign of the Second World War, which decided whether Britain could be supplied.

reviewer_note: Least sure: loss figures differ by source (Canadian War Museum: more than 3,000 Allied ships; Battle of the Atlantic Story: 3,500+ ships), so only the Canadian War Museum figure is used. The point is the middle of the North Atlantic, not a single site. D-Day link is only thematic.

beats.caption: The first convoy sails from Halifax for the United Kingdom, starting the escorted crossings that the campaign was fought over.
In March 1943, at the height of the battle, 108 Allied ships are sunk and 16 U-boats destroyed.
Strong convoy defence in May 1943 forces Germany to change U-boat strategy in the North Atlantic, the turning point of the battle.
